title: The Grant Nobody Told Her About

body.en: For two years, Patience assumed climate finance — grants, low-interest loans, resilience funds — was something only large companies or NGOs could access. Then a friend mentioned a small grants programme aimed specifically at women-led farming businesses adapting to erratic rainfall. Patience almost didn't apply, certain she wouldn't qualify. She did anyway. Six weeks later, she had funding to install a simple drip-irrigation system, cutting her dependence on unpredictable rain by more than half. The money had been sitting there the whole time. What was missing wasn't the funding. It was knowing it existed, and believing it was meant for someone like her.

followUpQuestion: What almost stopped Patience from applying for the grant, even though she was eligible?
